# At EAFIT we join in the celebration of World Youth Skills Day

**On this anniversary, celebrated on July 15, the United Nations General Assembly proposes to highlight the essential role of educators in training young people for their transition to the labor market and for their participation within their communities.**

**EAFIT, with the recent transformation of its Institutional Educational Project (PEI), has sought to contribute to the connection of the university community with the environment through the pedagogical model of active learning and the creation of alliances with companies, public systems and impact ventures.**

- [Start](https://www.eafit.edu.co/)
- [News](https://www.eafit.edu.co/noticias)
- At EAFIT we join in the celebration of World Youth Skills Day

![Image At EAFIT we join in the celebration of World Youth Skills Day](https://universidadeafit.widen.net/content/ccc050a5-d349-4f76-a513-fb90b123b6a0/web/Dia-Mundial-Habilidades.jpg?crop=yes&k=c&w=823&h=450&itok=7_eiJAi8)

The United Nations General Assembly has selected "Empowering teachers, trainers and young people for a transformative future" as the theme for World Youth Skills Day 2023.

The connection between hand and brain becomes essential when seeking to develop skills for solving challenges in different areas, as proposed by EAFIT's pedagogical model, which aligns with World Youth Skills Day. This commemoration was designated by the UN for July 15th, with the purpose of recognizing young people as agents of change and the need to provide them with the necessary training to overcome barriers to entering the workforce.

“At EAFIT, we join this important call to commemorate World Youth Skills Day. Let us encourage our young people to further develop their skills and build opportunities for the future. As the EAFIT community, we celebrate this day and honor it by doing what we do best: inspiring lives, creating knowledge, and transforming society,” says Claudia Restrepo Montoya, Rector of EAFIT University.

The role of institutions and educators is key to ensuring the development of relevant, flexible, and versatile skills in an era of technological advancements. María Paola Podestá Correa, Vice-Rector of Learning at the University, highlights skills such as critical thinking, effective communication, creativity, adaptability, and leadership, as well as technical skills such as computational thinking, business acumen, and the use of data analysis tools.

“In the case of universities, I believe that most of us are focused on connecting problems and solutions, and in this way reflecting in educational projects and learning systems the mechanisms to generate capacity for economic growth that manifests itself, for example, in an increase in employability through the creation of companies with added value,” the vice-rector points out.

Added to this is the changing dynamics of the labor market, where innovation is presented as a mandate, but beyond that, it is mainly about understanding and adapting to change, in connection with the reality of the actors involved.

EAFIT, in its Institutional Educational Project, promotes a series of competencies that seek, precisely, that the role of the teacher contributes to the current challenges from the generation of knowledge around problems, the understanding and management of technological tools, and social sensitivity.

“It is worth noting that the learning process always involves formulating questions about the conditions, interests, motivations and aspirations, from which it is possible to approach what, how and why to teach, and through what means, technologies and in what environments,” points out Adolfo Eslava Gómez, dean of the School of Arts and Humanities at EAFIT.

###### Young people and change

Youth unemployment is a pressing problem facing various economies and societies, according to the UN. While education and technical and vocational training play a fundamental role, young people are essential actors who need to be willing to value learning, adaptable, and curious to embrace change.

Julio Gil Valencia, leader of the Cosmo Schools Centro Experience Center, expresses that young people must assume a more critical and ethical role in relation to the power of technological, informational, communicative and digital structures, through guidance and a different educational proposal.

“When a boy or girl weaves their understanding of the world using new words, these new meanings broaden their horizons and give them more opportunities to build the world they want in terms of their autonomy. This will surely provide important tools for decision-making and reduce barriers to employment in the future,” Julio states.

This statement aligns with the vision of Gloria Figueroa Ortiz, CEO of the San José de Las Vegas Corporation, who recognizes the importance of working with younger generations. “I believe that intergenerational learning and collaboration are fundamental. Young people have so much to contribute, and it is crucial to be able to foster their creativity and their quick and agile ability to learn and adopt digital tools, combined with the opportunities that we, as adults, can offer them,” she says.

Estas consideraciones coinciden con la declaración que António Guterres, secretario general de la Asamblea General de las Naciones Unidos, comparte sobre esta efeméride: “Es esencial dotar a los jóvenes de una educación, formación y capacitación de calidad. Este Día Mundial de las Habilidades de la Juventud nos recuerda que los docentes se encuentran en la primera línea de este gran esfuerzo mundial".
